relationships.subject: Ultra-low dose naltrexone
relationships.evidence_quote: injection at the trigeminal ganglion (TG) or subnucleus caudalis (Sp5C) caused a significant reduction in heat hyperalgesia

relationships.subject: Ultra-low dose naltrexone
relationships.evidence_quote: Lipopolysaccharide (LPS) injection in the intraoral mucosa resulted in facial heat hyperalgesia an increase in IL-1β levels in the TG, which were reduced by systemic NTX.

relationships.subject: Ultra-low dose naltrexone
relationships.evidence_quote: suggest that blockade of TLR4 and downstream signaling pathway contribute to its effect

key_findings: Ultra-low dose naltrexone reduced postoperative orofacial hyperalgesia, acting at the trigeminal ganglion and Sp5C.
TLR4 blockade impeded the naltrexone effect and naltrexone reduced LPS-induced IL-1beta.
